claim: GitHub's required-reviews page says 'Pull request authors cannot approve their own pull requests' and that required approvals must come from people with write or admin permission. The protected-branches page says admins are exempt from a rule by default and that 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' applies the rule to admins; it also says force pushes are blocked on protected branches by default and that deletions are blocked by default. For a solo owner whose Claude sessions authenticate as the same admin account (verified 2026-10-07: pull request #2 was opened by gh0stl0nely and that account has admin permission), a rule needing 1 or more approvals locks everyone out, so the workable rule is: require a pull request with 0 approvals, block force pushes and deletions, do not allow bypassing. That rule does NOT stop a session merging its own pull request, because the same account may press merge. Only the Guardian hooks, or a second GitHub account used only by review sessions with approvals set to 1 (its token is an R5 step for the owner), do. The fetched protected-branches page does not say whether 0 approvals is allowed; the owner must confirm the 0-approval setting on screen.
